system_overview: This specification models the Transaction Commit protocol, which defines the requirements for a set of resource managers participating in a distributed transaction to reach agreement on whether to commit or abort. It captures the fundamental safety properties that any transaction commit implementation (such as two-phase commit or Paxos commit) must satisfy.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a finite set of resource managers (RMs), each of which independently decides whether to prepare (vote to commit) or abort. There is no explicit coordinator; the specification describes the allowed behaviors of the resource managers themselves.
state_variables: The system tracks a single mapping from each resource manager to its current state, which can be one of four values: working (initial, has not yet voted), prepared (voted to commit), committed (final commit decision), or aborted (final abort decision).
initial_state: Every resource manager starts in the working state.
actions: Two types of actions can occur for each resource manager: (1) Prepare: A resource manager that is currently working transitions to the prepared state, indicating it votes to commit. (2) Decide: A resource manager makes a final decision. It may commit if it is prepared and every resource manager in the system is either prepared or already committed. It may abort if it is working or prepared and no resource manager has yet committed. These conditions ensure that a commit decision is only possible when all participants have prepared, and an abort is only possible before any participant has committed.
safety_properties: Type correctness: every resource manager is always in one of the four valid states. Consistency: it is impossible for one resource manager to be in the aborted state while another is in the committed state. Together these guarantee that all resource managers that reach a final decision agree on the outcome.
model_bounds: The set of resource managers is declared as a constant. For model checking, it is typically instantiated with a small finite set such as three resource managers.
additional_assumptions: The specification describes only safety properties. It does not require that any action eventually be taken (no fairness conditions). The specification serves as a correctness criterion: more detailed protocols such as two-phase commit are shown to implement this specification via refinement.
